review_candidates.title: REMOTE - Vice President of Business Development
review_candidates.description: Company Description M3 Wake Research, an M3USA Company, is an integrated network of premier investigational sites meeting the clinical research needs of global biopharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical device, pharmaceutical and clinical research organizations (CROs). With close to 30 owned and managed research sites across the country, M3 Wake Research is one of the largest independent, multi-site clinical research companies in the US. M3 Wake Research continues to grow through acquisitions and uncompromising commitment to careful planning and execution in accordance with regulatory compliance. Conducting studies since 1984, M3 Wake Research owns a proprietary patient database of potential clinical trial participants across the US. As of today, our board-certified physicians have completed more than 7,000+ successful clinical trials, while consistently exceeding sponsor expectations for integrity, timeliness, subject enrollment, human protection, and expeditious delivery of accurate evaluable data. Due to our continued growth, we are hiring for a Vice President of Business Development at Wake Research, an M3 company. This is a remote position with up to 50% domestic-travel. Job Description The Vice President of Business Development is a key revenue-driving executive responsible for defining and leading enterprise-level growth strategy across the M3 Wake Research's network. Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer, this leader oversees new business acquisition, expansion of existing CRO and sponsor partnerships, and optimization of study volume across all sites. The role partners closely with Clinical Operations, Clinical Affairs, Marketing, Regulatory, Quality, Finance, and HR to ensure integrated planning and flawless execution. This position will shape market positioning, build a scalable and high-performing BD organization, and ensure the company is consistently recognized as a preferred site network partner in the clinical research industry. What You’ll Do Develop and execute comprehensive, data-driven sales strategies in alignment with the CEO to drive study awards and revenue growth. Penetrate high-value pharmaceutical, biotech, and CRO accounts to establish long-term, strategic partnerships that increase study volume and preferred-partner positioning. Expand business with existing clients by identifying growth opportunities, leading account strategy, and enhancing account performance. Conduct ongoing market and competitive analysis to identify emerging opportunities and inform strategic direction. Represent the organization at conferences, sponsor summits, and industry events to elevate visibility and expand key relationships. Partner with Marketing to develop campaigns that highlight PI expertise, patient access, site capabilities, and network strengths. Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing Business Development team with clear expectations, KPIs, and accountability structures. Recruit top business development talent and oversee territory and account allocation aligned with organizational priorities. Conduct regular 1:1s, mid-year and annual performance reviews, and ongoing assessments to ensure team success. Maintain accurate forecasts, pipeline metrics, and activity reporting through the CRM. Present performance insights and strategic recommendations to senior leadership. Manage special initiatives or strategic projects as assigned by the CEO. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree required; BA/BS in Business, Marketing, or Life Sciences preferred. MBA highly desirable. 7–10+ years of progressive sales experience within a clinical research site network or comparable research environment. Demonstrated success securing multi-site study opportunities with pharmaceutical sponsors, CROs, and biotech organizations. Established executive-level relationships across CRO and sponsor communities. Deep understanding of clinical research operations, feasibility, timelines, and site dynamics. Proven ability to build, scale, and lead high-performing BD teams. Strong communication, negotiation, and executive presentation skills. Proficiency with CRM platforms (Salesforce.com preferred). Ability to work autonomously and thrive in a fast-paced, evolving environment. Strategic mindset with analytical and data-driven decision-making capability. Exceptional relationship management and consultative selling skills. High accountability and ownership of targets. Strong cross-functional collaboration and partnership-building abilities. Ability to juggle competing priorities and adapt rapidly to change. Commitment to excellence, continuous improvement, and operational rigor. Additional Information About M3: M3 USA is at the forefront of healthcare innovation, offering digital solutions across healthcare, life sciences, pharmaceuticals, and more. Since our inception in 2000, we’ve seen remarkable growth, fueled by our mission to utilize the internet for a healthier world and more efficient healthcare systems. Our success is anchored in our trusted digital platforms that engage physician communities globally, facilitating impactful medical education, precise job placement, and insightful market research. M3 USA prides itself on a dynamic and innovative work environment where every team member contributes to global health advancements. Joining M3 USA means being part of a dedicated team striving to make a significant difference in healthcare. We provide a unique opportunity for you to be at the cutting edge of healthcare innovation, shaping the future in a meaningful career. Embrace the chance to drive change with M3 USA. Benefits A career opportunity with M3 Wake Research offers competitive wages, and benefits such as: 401(k), 401(k) matching Dental insurance Disability insurance Employee assistance program Flexible spending account Health insurance Life insurance Paid time off Vision insurance M3 reserves the right to change this job description to meet the business needs of the organization

review_candidates.description: DEADLINE FOR APPLICATIONS 12 November 2026-23:59-GMT+01:00 West Africa Standard Time (Kinshasa) WFP celebrates and embraces diversity. It is committed to the principle of equal employment opportunity for all its employees and encourages qualified candidates to apply irrespective of race, colour, national origin, ethnic or social background, genetic information, gender, gender identity and/or expression, sexual orientation, religion or belief, HIV status or disability. ABOUT WFP The World Food Programme is the world’s largest humanitarian organization saving lives in emergencies and using food assistance to build a pathway to peace, stability and prosperity, for people recovering from conflict, disasters and the impact of extreme weather shocks. At WFP, people are at the heart of everything we do and the vision of the future WFP workforce is one of diverse, committed, skilled, and high performing teams, selected on merit, operating in a healthy and inclusive work environment, living WFP's values (Integrity, Collaboration, Commitment, Humanity, and Inclusion) and working with partners to save and change the lives of those WFP serves. To learn more about WFP, visit our website: https://www.wfp.org and follow us on social media to keep up with our latest news: YouTube, LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, Twitter, TikTok. WHY JOIN WFP? WFP is a 2020 Nobel Peace Prize Laureate. WFP offers a highly inclusive, diverse, and multicultural working environment. WFP invests in the personal & professional development of its employees through a range of training, accreditation, coaching, mentorship, and other programs as well as through internal mobility opportunities. A career path in WFP provides an exciting opportunity to work across the various country, regional and global offices around the world, and with passionate colleagues who work tirelessly to ensure that effective humanitarian assistance reaches millions of people across the globe. We offer an attractive compensation package (please refer to the Terms and Conditions section of this vacancy announcement). Job Title: Protection from Sexual Abuse and Exploitation (PSEA) Officer Contract Type : International Consultant Level: Level II Duty Station: Kinshasa, DRC Duration: 11-months BACKGROUND: The Democratic Republic of the Congo continues to face a major food security crisis. Around 26.6 million people faced crisis-level or worse acute food insecurity nationwide in 2026. Women and children, internally displaced persons, returnees, rural households and communities affected by conflict and recurrent shocks are particularly vulnerable, especially in the eastern provinces. WFP has a Zero Tolerance Policy to SEA and recognizes that it is a gross violation of power and a form of gender-based violence that all humanitarian partners have to prevent and respond to. One of the gravest violations of these standards and obligations is the sexual exploitation and abuse (SEA) of beneficiaries by humanitarian actors. SEA is an exploitation of positions of power to seek and/or receive sexual favours or benefits in exchange for humanitarian services. WFP is committed to ensuring that the community rights to dignity, respect and integrity are protected and met. Under the direct supervision of the Deputy Country Director, the Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) Advisor will support WFP DRC to implement the WFP Zero Tolerance to SEA Policy. The PSEA Advisor will develop and implement the WFP DRC PSEA Action Plan, which focuses on scaling up and taking forward prevention and response efforts to sexual exploitation and abuse. This will include conceptualizing and implementing PSEA prevention activities, responding to alleged PSEA cases that are reported, and ensuring appropriate victim support, liaising with the PSEA Strategic Advisory Group and other inter-agency bodies addressing PSEA and making contributions to inter-agency PSEA response and monitoring, liaising with senior management at national, regional and international levels on the same. The PSEA Advisor will be also responsible for designing and implementing targeted capacity building activities for staff and partners across different sectors, producing and disseminating relevant technical guidance, tools and resources. REPORTING LINE: The position of PSEA Advisor (CST II) reports to the Deputy Country Director – Enabling Services, with cross-functional work with other units, namely Programme, Monitoring & Evaluation, and VAM. ACCOUNTABILITIES/RESPONSIBILITIES: Key Responsibilities PSEA Risk Assessment – Undertake a comprehensive risk assessment of WFP presence, operations and activities to identify existing and emerging risks and present mitigations for adoption by the Country Office. Identified risks and mitigations should also be integrated into relevant risk documents in Country Office and in programme and operational approaches – including in Human Resourcing. Action Plan and Standard Operating Procedure – Update the Country Office PSEA Action Plan that reflects and responds to current country context and WFP capacities across all areas of WFP (including Supply Chain, Programme and Human Resources). The Action Plan should be complemented by a costed implementation plan. The advisor will also be responsible to review and update the existing Standard Operating Procedure for Responding to Allegations of SEA in DRC Country Operations. The SOP should reflect clear roles and responsibilities, resources and community preferences and feedback on WFP prevention, mitigation, response and support. Survivor – centred approach – In collaboration with the community and other humanitarian stakeholders, advocate for a PSEA activities that are survivor-centred and responsive. This may include advocating for increased resources, strengthening referral mechanisms and strengthening capacity of WFP, Cooperating Partner, Community and other stakeholders to meet survivor-centred good practice. Interagency Collaboration – Represent WFP in the Strategic Advisory Group ensuring the needs of WFP’s affected population are addressed in the interagency forum, plans and outputs. The advisor will also be responsible for ensuring alignment between WFP and Interagency practice on risk, prevention, mitigation, response and support including alignment with community-based complaint mechanisms. Partner capacity – Oversee the implementation of the Interagency PSEA Partner Assessment Tools (developed by IASC with WFP support). Assessments should include partner capacity support plans and be periodically reviewed to ensure achievement of capacity needs and to reflect any context and partner changes. Where possible, interagency collaboration should be adopted to streamline assessments and support plans. Mainstreaming of PSEA – Identify existing good practice, gaps and opportunities for mainstreaming of PSEA across all WFP programmes and activities and support progress accordingly. This may require resource mobilisation, capacity building, strengthened interagency collaboration and enhanced referral pathways. This should be delivered in collaboration with related cross-cutting topics including protection, gender, accountability to affected populations and monitoring and evaluation. PSEA Focal Points – Develop a network of WFP DRC PSEA Focal Points ensuring roles and responsibilities are well understood and performed and that capacity development needs and opportunities are regularly reviewed and delivered. This includes ensuring that all Focal Points are able to collaborate with interagency PSEA networks in their location to establish Community Based Complaint Mechanisms and that SOPs for Interagency and WFP complaint handling is achieved within a survivor-centred standard. Awareness raising – The Advisor will be responsible for developing awareness raising approaches that are innovative and reflect the roles and responsibilities of the audience and their communication, information and language needs and preferences. This includes awareness raising of: WFP staff, CP staff, vendors and contractors, authorities and local leaders, community and other key stakeholders. Reporting - Support and advise Management on the reporting of SEA allegations through corporate mechanisms; ensure SEA reporting mechanism and protocols are clearly understood by all staff and implementing partners. Once a complaint is received, ensure that all information pertaining to complaints and reporting is handled and referred strictly in line with agreed protocols and the established global SOPs in place, both within WFP and at an interagency level. Key Deliverables One PSEA Risk Assessment Report finalized including identifying risks, mitigation measures and key entry points across WFP operations. One updated PSEA Action Plan with a costed implementation plan and timelines. Finalization of CP capacity assessment for all CPs and ensure capacity strengthening implementation plans are developed and followed up. A functional network of trained PSEA Focal Points established across all WFP DRC offices and field locations, with clear roles and responsibilities defined in official TORs. Capacity building activities and awareness sessions as identified conducted and learning reports prepared. Monthly reporting to management. QUALIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCE REQUIRED: Education: Advanced University degree in social sciences, psychology, public health, law or related. Additional training in relevant field desirable. Experience: At least eight (8) years of experience in PSEA, gender, Protection, GBV or related areas. Knowledge & Skills: Demonstrated knowledge of working with communities in deep-field locations. Proven integrity, objectivity and professional competence. Demonstrated sensitivity to cultural diversity and gender issues. Strong familiarity with UN policies and practices around gender, PSEA, Protection, GBV and related issues. Excellent research and analytical skillsExcellent writing and interpersonal skills. Demonstrated ability to lead and motivate multi-cultural, cross-functional teams. Languages: Fluency in oral and written English and French. Understanding of Swahili would be an advantage. If you require a reasonable accommodation, please contact: global.inclusion@wfp.org NO FEE DISCLAIMER The United Nations does not charge any application, processing, training, interviewing, testing or other fee in connection with the application or recruitment process. Therefore, you are advised to apply particular care when submitting personal information on the web. REMINDERS BEFORE YOU SUBMIT YOUR APPLICATION All applications must be submitted exclusively through our online recruiting system. We do not consider CVs or applications sent by email, LinkedIn, or any other channel. We strongly recommend that your Workday profile is accurate and complete, and that all sections are filled in, including your employment history, academic qualifications, language skills, and UN grade (if applicable). Once your profile is completed, please apply, and submit your application. If you experience technical issues while submitting your application, you may contact us at global.hrerecruitment@wfp.org. Please note that this email is only for technical issues with an application - unsolicited applications or documents sent to this inbox will not receive a reply. At the application stage, the only required documents are your CV and Cover Letter. Additional documents (passport, certificates, recommendation letters, etc.) may be requested later in the process. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted and invited to proceed to the next stage of the recruitment process. All employment decisions are made on the basis of organizational needs, job requirements, merit, and individual qualifications. WFP is committed to providing an inclusive work environment free of sexual exploitation and abuse, all forms of discrimination, any kind of harassment, sexual harassment, and abuse of authority. Therefore, all selected candidates will undergo rigorous reference and background checks. Review and provide medical input to the protocol and protocol training materials. Conduct training for the project team concerning the disease/therapeutic area, study design, and procedures. If applicable, attend and participate in Investigator Meetings. Provide consultation and support decisions relating to inclusion/exclusion criteria deviations for subject eligibility or other protocol-related questions. Provide telephone and online (email) coverage for emergency medical guidance outside of normal business hours. Ensure all protocol inquiries and answers are documented in the centralized tracker/CTMS. Review listings, laboratory reports, and subject profiles as outlined in the Medical Monitoring Plan and Safety Management Plan. Provide review of study protocols and on-going medical oversight of clinical trials to ensure that safety concerns and/or adverse events (AEs) are identified and appropriate responses to such concerns are developed and executed. Review safety data including serious adverse events (SAEs), laboratory data, medical history, and concomitant medications to assess patient risk or trends/signals of safety issues. Provide consultation to the study team during review of out-of-range laboratory values for clinical/protocol significance. Provide medical advice to the internal Pharmacovigilance/Drug Safety team on queries relating to the SAE case assessment and reporting for the trial. Provide reviews of subject narratives, periodic and interim safety reports, and other study related documentation. Assist with medical review of MedDRA-coded terms for AEs and medical histories, and WHODrug coded terms for concomitant medications/therapies. Review the Statistical Analysis Plans; tables, figures, and listings; and the Clinical Study Reports (CSRs), as needed. Ensure compliance with company Standard Operating Procedures and working practices for clinical trial safety medical monitoring. At least 10-15 years of experience in clinical development, with a strong background in medical monitoring, clinical trial oversight, and pharmacovigilance.
